issue162.title: [Audit] LIMS workflow, QC and repeat-testing implementation plan (Oct 2026)
issue162.body:
Tracking issue for the October 2026 end-to-end audit of SoilFER-LIMS (reception → preparation → workbench → QC → review → repeats → report → export). Audited at `main` @ `477cc1f`.

Each child issue below is self-contained: findings with file:line evidence, the exact change, edge cases, out-of-scope notes, guardrails and acceptance criteria. Open **one PR per issue**, with `Closes #N` in the description.

## How we work (audit gate)

1. **Codex** works the sub-issues in the checklist order below. Phase 0 comes first: those items are independent, so do the P0 ones first. Then #219 (policy settings) at the start of Phase 1. Respect each issue's "Depends on" line. Open **one PR per issue** with `Closes #N`, using branch `audit/<key>-<short-name>` and title `[Audit <key>] ...`.
2. Before starting an item, rebase on `main` and confirm the cited lines still show the problem. Line numbers are from `477cc1f`.
3. When a PR is ready and CI is green, add the label **`ready-for-audit`** and comment `@claude ready for audit at <head SHA>`.
4. **Claude** audits the PR against the issue's acceptance criteria and replies on the PR with either **`Audit passed: OK to merge and deploy`** or **`Audit failed`**, followed by the gaps.
5. **Merge and deploy only after a pass on the current head SHA.** Any push after a pass needs a new audit.
6. After deploying, comment on the issue `Deployed <merge SHA> to production at <time UTC>`, with the health-check output.
7. Claude runs a post-deploy check, then either closes the issue or comments what regressed. Codex does not close audit issues. Claude never merges or deploys.
8. Questions about an issue go as comments on that issue. Ask rather than guess on QC limits or data-model choices.

## Multi-lab principle: no hard-coded lab policy

SoilFER-LIMS may be deployed in hundreds of independent labs (accredited, working towards accreditation, teaching, field stations). **Every policy value is a per-lab setting with a shipped default.** This covers:

- batch size
- QC frequencies (blanks, duplicates, reference soil, CRMs, CCVs)
- acceptance limits
- whether QC blocks, warns or is advisory
- the reported-value rule
- repeat limits
- retention
- bench lock
- amendment rules
- report and sample number formats
- calculation variants

**How it is built (#219):**

- Labs pick a preset: `ISO17025_STRICT`, `BASIC` or `ADVISORY`.
- Labs can override individual keys, and per-method overrides sit on top.
- Every change is audited with a reason.
- Deployment profiles can ship different defaults.
- Each consuming issue reads its value from `policyService`. Inline literals are never allowed.

Scope-update comments were added on #165, #170, #177, #180, #185, #186, #187, #191, #192, #199, #202, #207, #210, #211, #214 and #216. They take precedence over those issue bodies.

### Shipped defaults (Strict preset)

| Setting | Strict (default) | Basic | Advisory |
|---|---|---|---|
| QC mode | missing/failed QC blocks | flag, don't block | optional, shown only |
| Max samples per analytical batch | 20 | 40 | none |
| Duplicate frequency | 1 per 10 samples, min 1 | 1 per 20 | off |
| In-house reference soil (LRM) | every batch, control-chart limits after ≥ 20 points | off | off |
| CRM frequency | every 10th batch | off | off |
| Reported value when duplicates agree | mean (within repeatability r) | mean | latest valid |
| Max attempts before NCR | 3 | 5 | no limit |
| Sample retention after report | 90 days | 60 | 30 |
| Bench idle lock | 5 min, PIN at Record | 15 min | off |
| Values between LOD and LOQ | "< LOQ" | "< LOQ" | value, flagged |
| Amendment needs a second person | yes | yes | no |

YY can still change these defaults, and doing so does not block any phase.

## QC design and Repeat design (reference for Phase 2, 3, 7 issues)

### Practice this is based on (plan §3.1)

- **ISO/IEC 17025:2017.**
  - §7.7 (ensuring validity of results): the lab must monitor validity using reference materials or QC materials, replicate tests, retesting of retained items, blanks, intermediate checks of equipment, and interlaboratory comparison/PT. Data must be recorded so trends are detectable and, where practicable, statistical techniques must be applied. When results fall outside pre-defined criteria, planned action must prevent incorrect results being reported.
  - §7.5: technical records must include raw observations and calculations and must be traceable to who did them and when, with original values kept when amended.
  - §7.8.8: amended reports must be identified as such, carry the reason, and reference the report they replace.
  - §7.10: nonconforming work.
- **GLOSOLAN QA/QC guidance (FAO GSP) and SOP practice.**
  - Each analytical batch carries a reagent/method blank.
  - A duplicate is analysed on roughly 5–10 % of samples.
  - A laboratory (in-house) reference soil is analysed in every batch and charted on Shewhart charts.
  - CRMs/PT materials are used periodically to establish trueness.
  - Participation in GLOSOLAN proficiency testing.
- **Typical commercial soil-lab and EPA-style practice for instrumental methods (ICP-OES, AAS, UV-Vis).**
  - Calibration curve with acceptance (r ≥ 0.995).
  - Initial calibration verification (ICV, second source).
  - Continuing calibration verification (CCV) every 10–20 readings and at the end (90–110 %).
  - Calibration blank (CCB).
  - If a CCV fails, samples bracketed since the last passing CCV are re-run.
- **Statistical QC.**
  - Shewhart charts: warning limits ±2 s, action limits ±3 s, from at least 20 in-control points.
  - Westgard multirules:
    - 1-2s warning
    - 1-3s reject
    - 2-2s reject
    - R-4s reject
    - 4-1s / 10x review for bias or drift
  - Limits are fixed by the QA manager and re-derived deliberately, not continuously.
- **Duplicates near the detection limit.** RPD is meaningless when values are close to LOQ. Use an absolute difference criterion below about 5× LOQ.
- **Repeatability rule for replicates (ISO 5725-6 style).**
  - If |x1 − x2| ≤ r (the method repeatability limit), report the mean.
  - Otherwise take a third measurement and apply the range rule for n = 3, or investigate.

### QC design: decisions (plan §3.2; shipped defaults of the Strict preset, configurable per lab and per method via #219 and #185)

| QC element | What it is in the system | Default frequency | Default acceptance | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method blank (MB) | QC position in the run, entered like a sample | 1 per batch, at start (2 for batches > 20) | measured < LOQ of the method (or < ½ LOQ when configured) | Batch → `QC_FAIL` for that analyte. Re-run batch, or manager accepts with deviation if all samples are > 10× blank |
| Analytical duplicate (DUP) | Second replicate of a *real* sample in the batch, system-picked (random) or technician-picked | 1 per 10 samples, minimum 1 per batch | both ≥ 5×LOQ: RPD ≤ method limit (default 10 %; pH: \|Δ\| ≤ 0.2 units; texture: \|Δ\| ≤ 3 % per fraction). Otherwise \|Δ\| ≤ LOQ | Duplicate pair `FAIL` → batch `QC_FAIL` (configurable: warning only for the sample) |
| Laboratory reference material / check soil (LRM) | QC position linked to a `ReferenceMaterial` lot (in-house soil) | 1 per batch | Within control-chart limits: ±3 s action, ±2 s warning, plus Westgard rules. Fixed window (e.g. ±10 %) until ≥ 20 points exist | 1-3s, 2-2s or R-4s → `QC_FAIL`. 1-2s → warning. 10x → QA review task |
| Certified reference material (CRM) | QC position linked to a certified `ReferenceMaterial` lot | Configurable (default every 10th batch or monthly per method) | \|x − certified\| ≤ 2·√(u_lab² + u_cert²) (equivalently \|En\| ≤ 1). Recovery window as fallback | `QC_FAIL` + nonconformity (trueness) |
| Calibration verification (ICV/CCV) and calibration blank (CCB), instrumental methods only | QC positions inside the run sequence | ICV at start; CCV + CCB every N (default 10) samples and at the end | CCV 90–110 % (configurable); CCB < LOQ | Samples bracketed since the last passing CCV become `REPEAT_REQUIRED`. Not the whole batch |
| Calibration curve | Run-level record (points, slope, intercept, r) | Each run | r ≥ 0.995, ≥ 5 points (configurable) | Run cannot be committed |
| Proficiency testing | Existing `ProficiencyRound` | Per scheme | \|z\| ≤ 2 satisfactory, 2 < \|z\| < 3 questionable, \|z\| ≥ 3 unsatisfactory | Unsatisfactory → mandatory corrective action record |

Batch rules:
- An **analytical batch** (run) is the unit of QC acceptance. It covers one method, one instrument, one analyst session, and at most N samples (default 20, configurable per method).
- A batch's QC verdict is **per analyte**. For example, an ICP run covering Ca, Mg, K and Na can pass Ca and fail K.
- **Reported value with duplicates.** For a sample that has a duplicate in the batch, report the **mean** when the pair passes. Store both replicates. Report rounding follows `decimalPlaces` of the method.
- **Blank correction.** Optional per method (`blankCorrection: NONE | SUBTRACT_MEAN_BLANK`). When enabled, the raw and corrected values are both stored.
- **LOD/LOQ.**
  - Stored per methodology.
  - Optionally re-estimated from blank history (LOD = 3 s_blank, LOQ = 10 s_blank) through a QA-manager action that creates a new methodology revision. Never automatic.
  - Values between LOD and LOQ are reported as "< LOQ" by default (configurable to "trace").

### Repeat design (plan §3.3)

Concepts (re-using and fixing existing tables):

- **Test**: `OrderLine` (what was ordered) ↔ `WorkItem` (the job). One WorkItem per sample × analysis, kept.
- **Attempt**: `WorkAttempt`. One execution of the test in one batch. An attempt holds 1..n replicate measurements (`Result` rows with `replicateNo`), raw data, instrument and batch. Every repeat is a **new attempt** (`attemptNo + 1`). Old attempts are never modified, except for their status.
- **Reported value**: chosen per test from the attempts by an explicit, recorded selection (`ReportedValueSelection`), never by "latest row wins".

Repeat reason codes (enum `RepeatReason`):

| Code | Triggered by | Original attempt becomes | Default reported value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QC_BATCH_FAIL` | System, on batch disposition REANALYZE, or CCV bracket failure | `INVALIDATED` | New attempt |
| `REVIEW_OUTLIER` | Reviewer: implausible value, or cross-parameter check failed | `QUESTIONED` | Reviewer chooses: ORIGINAL, REPEAT, or MEAN if \|Δ\| ≤ r |
| `DUPLICATE_DISAGREEMENT` | System: the sample's own duplicate failed | `QUESTIONED` | Third replicate; ISO 5725 range rule |
| `ABOVE_RANGE_DILUTION` | Technician or system (value > calibration range) | `INVALIDATED` | New attempt (with dilution factor) |
| `INSTRUMENT_FAULT` / `PREP_ERROR` | Technician (before submit) or reviewer | `INVALIDATED` | New attempt |
| `TRANSCRIPTION_ERROR` | Technician or reviewer | Corrected by a **correction** of the same attempt (old value kept in the audit trail, reason mandatory). No new measurement | Corrected value |
| `CLIENT_RETEST` | Manager, after approval/report | Stays `ACCEPTED` | Requires a `SampleAmendment`. Reviewer chooses; the amended report shows both if policy says so |
| `CONFIRMATION` | Reviewer (e.g. sum of bases > CEC) | `QUESTIONED` | Reviewer chooses |

Rules:
1. A repeat always creates a new attempt, which must be measured in a **different batch** from a failed one. The server refuses to attach a repeat attempt to a batch whose QC was `QC_FAIL` or whose disposition was REANALYZE/REJECT.
2. A repeat needs a reason code. Free-text notes are optional, except for `OTHER`, which requires them.
3. A technician can start a repeat themselves before submission (`INSTRUMENT_FAULT`, `PREP_ERROR`, `ABOVE_RANGE_DILUTION`, `TRANSCRIPTION_ERROR`). After submission, only a reviewer or manager can.
4. Attempt limit: the default is 3 attempts per test. A 4th requires manager approval and opens a nonconformity record (`NonconformityReport`, see #193). The limit is the policy key `repeats.maxAttemptsBeforeNcr`.
5. The review screen shows all attempts side by side: value, batch, QC status, analyst, date, reason. The reviewer explicitly selects the reported value. Selection options: `ATTEMPT:<id>`, `MEAN_OF:<ids>` (allowed only when the spread is ≤ the repeatability limit r of the method), or `NOT_REPORTABLE` (with reason → WAIVE).
6. Reports and exports read **only** the selected reported value. Other attempts can optionally appear in a QC annex. They never appear as results.
7. A repeat after a report has been issued must go through an amendment (ISO §7.8.8). See #210.

issue190.body:
Part of the 2026-10 LIMS audit plan, **Phase 3: Attempts, repeats, reported value**, item **3.1**. Tracking issue: #162

Audited at `main` @ `477cc1f`. Paths given as a bare file name live under `server/controllers/`, `server/services/`, `server/utils/`, `server/routes/` or `client/src/components/...`. Line numbers may have moved; if a line doesn't match, search for the quoted symbol and confirm the problem still exists before changing anything.

The repeat design this implements (reason codes, attempt rules, reported-value selection) is in tracking issue #162, section "Repeat design". Follow it unless this issue says otherwise.

## Problem (audit findings)

- **D2** (P0): DataSheet/status path writes only `WorkItem.result`, so the reviewed value differs from the reported one
  - Evidence: `workItemController.js:899,1084-1110,1246`; `client/src/pages/DataSheet.jsx:64,81`; `SampleDetail.jsx:332`; `workflowContract.js:83`
- **D15** (P2): Values and flags mutated in place. `undoApproval` makes illegal bulk transitions, hard-deletes post-analytical items, is non-transactional, and does not withdraw the issued report
  - Evidence: `workItemController.js:1088`; `qcService.js:383-431`; `sampleController.js:2283-2334`
- **D16** (P2): Status strings are inconsistent (`REJECTED`, `RELEASED`, `WAIVE`, `REJECT_REANALYSIS`, `REVIEWED`). `reviewWorkItem` doesn't set `reviewedBy`/`reviewedAt`
  - Evidence: `qcController.js:889,900`; `exchangePolicyService.js:166`; `schema.prisma:1153`; `submissionController.js:425`
- **B19** (P2): Replicates are unusable. Replicate is a dropdown, and recording locks the row, so replicate 2 cannot be entered. No mean or RPD
  - Evidence: `WorkbenchInspector.jsx:175-184`; `WorksheetArea.jsx:305,432`

Scope pin for #211: analysis identity. **Your adaptation is accepted. No separate stable-identity migration is required before #211.**

On main, `Analysis.code` is the `@id` (schema.prisma:1299-1300), and the existing relations reference it with `onDelete: Restrict`. That makes it the stable analysis identity this rule needs. "Stable analysis id" in pin 6097307274 means that primary key, not a display name, alias or label.

1. **New report items** freeze `analysisId` = the `Analysis.code` primary key, captured at generation from the same source the item's value came from (`ReportedValueSelection.analysisCode` / the frozen `param`).
2. **Historical predecessors** without `analysisId` use their already-frozen `param`, verbatim, as that key. There is no rewrite, backfill or normalisation of stored report content.
3. **Comparison** is exact string equality on the key. There is no case-folding, trimming, alias, name or catalogue lookup. A legacy code that no longer exists in the catalogue still compares normally, because the comparison never resolves the catalogue.
4. **Missing identity.** If an item on either side has no usable identity (both `analysisId` and `param` are absent, empty or not a string), refuse with **409 `REPORT_AMENDMENT_EVIDENCE_INVALID`** and zero writes, as in pin 6097307274 point 4. The error details name the report and item position, but no values.
5. No new ids, no catalogue renumbering, no new identity table and no migration of existing rows. Any later move to a surrogate key belongs in its own issue, not #211.
6. **Tests required** (in addition to pin 6097307274):
   - a predecessor that only has `param`, paired with a new item that has `analysisId`;
   - a legacy code missing from the catalogue, still paired by exact key;
   - codes that differ only by case or whitespace, treated as different analyses;

issue253.title: QC runs: reviewed correction of transcription errors on failed runs
issue253.body:
Follow-up from #186 (pin part 11, PR #251).

**Why:** a QC_FAIL analyte is locked by #164. Only a disposition can move it: REPEAT_ORDERED, ACCEPTED_WITH_DEVIATION or REJECTED. That means a plain transcription error in a QC reading (a typo, not a real failure) can't be corrected on a failed run. The analyst has to repeat the run or accept it with a deviation.

**Change:** add a reviewed correction path for failed runs.
- A second person with APPROVE_RESULTS (not the analyst) approves the correction and gives a reason.
- It appends a superseding QcMeasurement through the existing corrections route, re-evaluates, and records a BatchEvent naming both people.
- The original reading and the failed evaluation stay visible in history and on reports.
- Per-lab policy decides whether the path is enabled (default off).

Classification is absent/add; present nullable TEXT with no default/already-present no-op; any differing type/nullability/default/refuse with a stable code and zero writes. Add Docker wiring after the existing additive installers and before guards which read `Result.rawInput`, including #193 and #197. Preserve the production-volume-independent DDL source path.

## Guardrails and edge cases

Every existing Result column and row stays identical. Historical rawInput remains NULL; never derive it from value or back-fill it. Preserve every existing migration/audit receipt. Hash mismatch and partial/wrong shapes refuse rather than repair. Do not change the literal disposable baseline or any readiness assertion. Do not relax #197's prerequisite check. No production host action under the demo freeze.

#182 is merged and already passed its production post-deploy check. This PR fixes only release wiring for its exact additive column. #197 must merge audited main after this PR merges, then rerun its own full CI and audit. No override-request model or analytical calculation changes here.
